SMTO-HTTP-0059 — The Agent didn't use the connection it already set up

GUID: 7d0349bd-40cc-493d-9298-34b8ca25c403
Slug: http-verified-route-required
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO had already set up a working connection to this service and expected the Agent's next step to use it. The Agent asked for something else, so SMTO stopped that step. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the Agent to continue. SMTO automatically tells it which connection to use and lets it correct itself up to two times. Most of the time the Agent fixes the step on its own without your help.
  2. If the Run stops, reply in the Conversation asking the Agent to reuse the connection it already set up for that service. A clear instruction points the Agent back to the connection that is already working.
  3. If you really want a different account or address, tell the Agent exactly which saved connection in Parameter Store to use instead. Using a different connection is allowed, but it has to be chosen on purpose.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's next web request goes through and its result appears in the Conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Nothing was sent to the other service, so you don't need to check it for changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The routing.http_reuse guard rejected the tool call because it was not the focused phase's tool (http.request or http.connect) or its arguments failed that phase's advertised schema; the call was recorded with executed=false.

What this means

  • The focused verified HTTP setup phase received a different tool call or arguments failing that phase's advertised schema. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The focused verified HTTP setup phase received a different tool call or arguments failing that phase's advertised schema.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the active route phase and focused tool schema; explicit alternate configuration follows its own normal checks.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the conversation.reuse_corrected event and expected_route in the Run. The model gets two correction attempts, after which the run is blocked with http_reuse_correction_limit. Use the advertised profile_key, connection_ref or http.connect recipe, or supply an explicit alternate configuration that passes the normal authentication and origin checks.
  • Follow the currently advertised HTTP setup/discovery phase and its verified route. An explicit alternate configuration must pass its ordinary authentication and origin checks.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The next accepted call matches the advertised phase or an intentional alternate route is validated normally.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
